key_insight: Adding an ADR physical PV efficiency model to TSMixer offers limited practical benefit for day-ahead solar power forecasting over the purely data-driven baseline.
engineering_relevance: For large-scale PV forecasting, the added complexity of physics-informed hybrid models may not yield better accuracy, geographic transferability, or data efficiency.
method: Combine the ADR physical PV efficiency model with TSMixer.
Test feature augmentation and residual-learning hybrid architectures.
Compare convergence, accuracy, geographic transferability, and limited-data performance.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on over 3 million samples from 3,713 PV installations across 33 European countries found slightly faster apparent convergence but no consistent gains in test accuracy, generalization, or limited-data performance.
watch_item: These findings concern ADR–TSMixer hybrids for day-ahead PV forecasting and should not be generalized to all physics-informed models or forecasting settings.
paper_title: The Utility of Physics-Informed Machine Learning in Solar Power Production Forecasting
